questions.q: Which of these is a brand of security (alarm) systems?
questions.ref: General telecommunications and structured-cabling practice (PABX, RJ11/RJ45)
questions.n: Visonic makes wireless alarm and security panels. Cisco = network equipment; Phelps Dodge = electrical wire and cable.

questions.q: What is the usual mix proportion (cement : sand : gravel) of Class AA concrete?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: Memory ladder: AA 1:1.5:3, A 1:2:4, B 1:2.5:5, C 1:3:6. The richer in cement, the higher the class.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a cleanout?
o: Gives access for inspecting and clearing blockages
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Revised), drainage and vent provisions
questions.n: A cleanout is a service door into the pipe. Plumbers push a snake through it.

questions.q: Which stain- and acid-resistant material is well suited to kitchen countertops?
questions.ref: General building-materials references (rocks, masonry, finishes)
questions.n: Sintered stone is fired at high heat and pressure, so it is dense and non-porous. Marble stains and etches with acids such as lemon juice.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of concrete cover over reinforcing bars?
o: Protects the steel from corrosion and fire and helps bond
To reduce the amount of cement
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: Cover is the concrete 'jacket' around the bars. Without it the steel rusts and swells, and the concrete spalls.

questions.q: In a steel frame, which element commonly connects the web of a beam to a column?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: A pair of angles bolts the beam end to the column like an L-bracket joining shelf and wall. In concrete frames the link is the beam-column joint with anchored rebars.

questions.q: Which glass door is commonly used for retail shops?
questions.ref: General glazing and glass-fabrication practice
questions.n: A frameless door shows the store inside with nothing in the way, like a window that opens.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a vent stack in the sanitary drainage system?
o: Equalizes air pressure to protect trap seals and lets sewer gases escape
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Revised), drainage and vent provisions
questions.n: A vent lets air in behind flowing water so traps do not get sucked dry. Like poking a second hole in a juice can so it pours smoothly.

questions.q: Which wall type is best for an acoustic room such as a recording studio?
o: Double wall with an air gap and insulation
questions.ref: General architectural-acoustics practice
questions.n: Two separate walls with insulation between them stop vibration from jumping across. Think of two doors with a hallway between them.

questions.q: Which cross-section shape usually goes with a spiral column?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: A helix wraps naturally around a round core.

questions.q: Where is single-phase power most commonly used?
questions.ref: Philippine Electrical Code and general residential wiring practice
questions.n: Lights, outlets, and small appliances run on single-phase. Big motors prefer three-phase.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a vent cap?
o: Lets air in and out while keeping rain, debris, and pests out of the vent pipe
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Revised), drainage and vent provisions
questions.n: It is a hat on the vent pipe's roof opening. Air passes; rain and birds do not.

questions.q: What treatment is used on a concrete floor to stop vibration and impact noise from being felt below?
questions.ref: General architectural-acoustics practice
questions.n: A floating floor sits on rubber-like pads, so vibration cannot pass straight into the slab. Like walking on a mattress instead of the ground.

questions.q: Which roof covering needs the most maintenance over time?
questions.ref: General roofing and roof-framing references
questions.n: Wood rots, curls, and burns. Memory trick: natural material, natural decay.

questions.q: What color is commonly used for the live wire in a single-phase circuit?
questions.ref: Philippine Electrical Code and general residential wiring practice
questions.n: Green or yellow-green is the ground. Blue (or white) is the neutral. Color codes vary by code edition, so confirm locally.

questions.q: What gives a seamless look to the joints of frameless glass panels?
questions.ref: General glazing and glass-fabrication practice
questions.n: Clear silicone fills and bonds the butt joint, so the glass looks like one sheet.

questions.q: Granite belongs to which rock family?
questions.ref: General building-materials references (rocks, masonry, finishes)
questions.n: Granite cools from molten rock deep underground. Igneous comes from Latin ignis, 'fire'. Think of cooled candle wax. Granite word root: Italian granito, 'grained'.

questions.q: Which element provides ductility to a reinforced concrete member?
o: Properly placed and sufficient steel reinforcement
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: Concrete is strong but brittle, like a cracker. Steel bars stretch before breaking, so they warn before failure. Word root: ductile from Latin ducere, 'to lead' (can be drawn out into wire).

questions.q: Which roofing material is the right choice for a standing seam roof?
questions.ref: General roofing and roof-framing references
questions.n: Standing seams are raised folded joints between metal panels. Wood and tile cannot be folded.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear opening of an accessible elevator door?
questions.ref: 2024 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of BP 344, NCDA/DPWH
questions.n: The door is narrower than the car, but 900 mm still clears a wheelchair. Word root: elevator from Latin elevare, 'to lift up'.

questions.q: How many live (line) wires does a three-phase circuit have?
questions.ref: Philippine Electrical Code and general residential wiring practice
questions.n: L1, L2, and L3 are the live wires. A neutral may be added, but it is not a live wire.

questions.q: What is the minimum thickness of a reinforced concrete footing measured above the bottom reinforcement, for footings on soil?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015, Sec. 305 (Footings) and Chapter 4 (footing depth above bottom reinforcement)
questions.n: 300 mm applies to footings on piles. Soil footings are the thinner case.

questions.q: What is the commonly used minimum size of main reinforcing bars in concrete members?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: 10 mm is the usual lower limit for structural main bars. Column main bars are bigger (16 mm).

questions.q: Which test measures the moisture content of soil?
questions.ref: General building-materials references (rocks, masonry, finishes)
questions.n: Weigh the sample, bake it, weigh again. The lost weight was water.

questions.q: Under NSCP Table 305-1, what is the minimum depth below undisturbed ground for the footing of a one-storey concrete foundation?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015, Sec. 305 (Footings) and Chapter 4 (footing depth above bottom reinforcement)
questions.n: Depth grows with floors: 1 floor 300 mm, 2 floors 450 mm, 3 floors 600 mm. Taller means deeper roots, like a tree.

questions.q: Which material expands when it contacts water and is used as a waterstop?
questions.ref: General waterproofing and moisture-protection practice
questions.n: Bentonite clay swells many times its size and plugs gaps. Word root: named after Fort Benton, Wyoming. Think of a dry sponge that fills any crack once wet.

questions.q: How many switches are used in a standard three-way switch circuit?
questions.ref: Philippine Electrical Code and general residential wiring practice
questions.n: Two switches control one light from two places, like the hallway light with a switch at each end.

questions.q: Which is the most commonly used sedimentary rock in construction?
questions.ref: General building-materials references (rocks, masonry, finishes)
questions.n: Sedimentary rock forms in layers, like a layer cake. Marble is limestone cooked into metamorphic rock.

questions.q: How many live (line) wires does a single-phase circuit have?
questions.ref: Philippine Electrical Code and general residential wiring practice
questions.n: Single-phase = one live wire plus a neutral (and a ground). Think of one supply pipe and one return pipe.

questions.q: Which room proportion is best for acoustics?
o: Unequal length, width, and height (not a cube)
questions.ref: General architectural-acoustics practice
questions.n: Equal dimensions pile up the same sound waves (standing waves). Uneven sizes spread them out.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the grab bar or handrail inside an accessible elevator?
o: To give support and balance to passengers, especially persons with disabilities
questions.ref: 2024 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of BP 344, NCDA/DPWH
questions.n: Elevators start and stop with a jolt. The rail is a steady hand when you are unsteady.

questions.q: Which window best fits a narrow hallway or stairwell where the only purpose is to let light in?
questions.ref: General glazing and glass-fabrication practice
questions.n: A fixed window does not open, so it needs no clearance. Operable windows would swing into the passage.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width of an accessible elevator car?
questions.ref: 2024 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of BP 344, NCDA/DPWH
questions.n: Memory trick: width 1200, depth 1400. The car is longer than it is wide.

questions.q: Which connector is commonly used for telephone lines in the Philippines?
questions.ref: General telecommunications and structured-cabling practice (PABX, RJ11/RJ45)
questions.n: RJ11 is the small 2-pair phone plug; RJ45 is the wider 4-pair network plug. Memory trick: 11 is thin like a phone cord, 45 is fat like a network cable.

questions.q: What is the standard minimum slope of horizontal sanitary drainage pipes?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Revised), drainage and vent provisions
questions.n: That is a drop of 20 mm over every meter, or 1/4 inch per foot.

questions.q: What is the minimum diameter of the main bars used in a tied column?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: Columns carry compression, so thin bars buckle. Ties are smaller (10 mm). Common NSCP-based practice.

questions.q: Which part of a fire detection and alarm system receives signals from detectors and triggers the alarm?
questions.ref: General fire-detection and alarm-system practice (FDAS)
questions.n: The FACP is the system's brain. Detectors are the senses. FDAS is the whole system; FACP is the control panel within it.

questions.q: Which part is used to seal the joint between two flanged pipe sections?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Revised), drainage and vent provisions
questions.n: A gasket is a soft ring squeezed between flanges to stop leaks, like the rubber ring in a jar lid.

questions.q: What is the difference between a tied column and a spiral column?
o: Spiral columns have no vertical bars
Tied columns are always round and spiral columns square
They are identical except for color
Tied columns use separate hoops with at least 4 bars; spiral columns use a continuous helix with at least 6 bars and are more ductile
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: Ties are separate rings, like barrel hoops. A spiral is one long coil, like a spring, so it confines the core better. Strength reduction factor: 0.65 tied, 0.75 spiral.

questions.q: Which device attaches pipes to a wall or ceiling?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Revised), drainage and vent provisions
questions.n: Clamps hold the pipe's weight, like a hook for a hose.

questions.q: What does PABX stand for?
questions.ref: General telecommunications and structured-cabling practice (PABX, RJ11/RJ45)
questions.n: A PABX is a building's own phone switchboard that shares a few outside lines among many desk phones. Word root: exchange = a place where calls are swapped between lines. Think of the office receptionist's switchboard, but automatic.

questions.q: Which roof type needs a stronger structure because of heavy foot traffic and maintenance access?
questions.ref: General roofing and roof-framing references
questions.n: A roof deck is a floor in the sky, so it must carry people, furniture, and equipment.

questions.q: According to design practice and NSCP checks, what minimum factor of safety against overturning is used for a gravity retaining wall?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: The wall's resisting moment must be 1.5 times the overturning moment. Similar value (1.5) is used for sliding.

questions.q: Which device covers the gap where a pipe passes through a wall?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Revised), drainage and vent provisions
questions.n: Word root: Old French escuchon, from Latin scutum, 'shield'. It is a small decorative shield around the hole.

questions.q: Which of these is a cementitious waterproofing coating?
questions.ref: General waterproofing and moisture-protection practice
questions.n: Cementitious coatings are cement-based and brushed on like thick paint, good for rigid surfaces such as tanks.

questions.q: Which section is used to hold glass edges onto a structural steel member?
questions.ref: General glazing and glass-fabrication practice
questions.n: A U-channel cradles the glass edge like a hand holding a plate.

questions.q: What curing method is used for concrete hollow blocks (CHB) when you need them to cure quickly?
questions.ref: General building-materials references (rocks, masonry, finishes)
questions.n: Heat and moisture speed up cement hydration, like a pressure cooker for blocks.

questions.q: In a roof truss, which member resists tension and keeps the rafters from spreading?
questions.ref: General roofing and roof-framing references
questions.n: The tie is the string on a bow: it pulls the two ends together.

questions.q: What is the purpose of mortar in masonry construction?
o: Bonds units together and spreads the load evenly
questions.ref: General building-materials references (rocks, masonry, finishes)
questions.n: Word root: Latin mortarium, a bowl for pounding. Mortar is the cushion between bricks, like the cream in a sandwich.

questions.q: When a 2% slope is impracticable, what reduced slope may a 100 mm (102 mm or larger) horizontal drain use if approved?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Revised), drainage and vent provisions
questions.n: Bigger pipes carry more water, so they can run flatter. The recall list did not give a key for 100 mm, so know both numbers: 2% standard, 1% reduced.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a beam in a slab-beam relationship?
o: It carries the slab load and transfers it to the columns
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: The slab rests on beams, and beams hand the load to columns. Think of beams as the shelves' brackets and columns as the wall posts.

questions.q: Which door is most effective for blocking sound?
questions.ref: General architectural-acoustics practice
questions.n: Mass blocks sound, and seals close the gaps. Word root: acoustics from Greek akouein, 'to hear'.

questions.q: What do you call the protection that resists water under pressure (hydrostatic pressure)?
questions.ref: General waterproofing and moisture-protection practice
questions.n: Waterproofing handles pressurized water, like a basement below the water table. Dampproofing only stops moisture and vapor.

questions.q: What is the typical angle of repose of dry loose granular material such as sand?
questions.ref: General building-materials references (rocks, masonry, finishes)
questions.n: It is the steepest slope a pile holds before sliding, like a sand pile at the beach.

questions.q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the minimum clear depth of an accessible elevator car?
questions.ref: 2024 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of BP 344, NCDA/DPWH
questions.n: Depth is the front-to-back length of the car. The car is 1400 mm deep and 1200 mm wide, so a wheelchair can enter and fit.

questions.q: What happens if the supporting beam is removed in a slab-beam system?
o: The slab span grows, so bending and deflection increase and the slab may crack or fail
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), reinforced concrete provisions and common design practice
questions.n: Longer span means more bend. Like removing the middle leg of a table: the top sags. A thicker slab or a flat-slab design would be needed.

questions.q: Which fitting joins two pipes of different sizes?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Revised), drainage and vent provisions
questions.n: A reducer steps a pipe down in size, like a funnel. A bushing also reduces size but fits inside another fitting.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a raised access floor system?
o: Easy access to cables and floor boxes without cutting the floor slab
To remove the need for an HVAC system
questions.ref: General telecommunications and structured-cabling practice (PABX, RJ11/RJ45)
questions.n: A raised floor leaves a void under removable panels for cables, so changes need no slab cutting. Think of a stage with a hollow under it where the wiring runs.
